summary: NASA's 3D model of the Space Shuttle at launch, cut into the orbiter, the external tank and the two boosters, colored, staging in a flight's order, much faster than real.

claims.claim: The two boosters go first, about two minutes after launch; the external tank goes after the main engines stop, about eight and a half minutes in; the orbiter flies on with its two maneuvering engines.
claims.how: The drive moves each piece at its time on a 12-second clock; the test checks the order and that the boosters fall away to both sides.

sources.title: Space Shuttle
sources.says: After expending their fuel, the SRBs were jettisoned approximately two minutes after launch... main engine cutoff (MECO), which occurred at T+8 minutes 30 seconds... the ET was jettisoned after main engine cutoff and just before orbit insertion, which used the orbiter's two Orbital Maneuvering System (OMS) engines.

sources.title: Space Shuttle external tank
sources.says: The ET was jettisoned just over 10 seconds after main engine cut-off (MECO).

claims.claim: The Shuttles flew 135 missions from 1981 to 2011, and the external tank was the only major part not reused.

sources.title: Space Shuttle
sources.says: Five complete Space Shuttle orbiter vehicles were built and flown on a total of 135 missions from 1981 to 2011... The ET was the only major component of the Space Shuttle system that was not reused.

claims.claim: The model is NASA's (NASA/Michael D. Carbajal), used under NASA's media guidelines, and carries no logo.
claims.how: The model has no texture; the test checks the GLB has no image or texture. Its cockpit windows' frames (132 tiny meshes) are left out.

sources.title: Images and media usage guidelines
sources.says: NASA content (images, audio, video, and computer files used in the rendition of 3-dimensional models...) generally are not subject to copyright in the United States.

simplified: Staging that took minutes is shown in 12 seconds.
The orbiter's black and white tiles are drawn simply: black below the wings, white above.
The boosters are not shown parachuting into the sea.
